interfaces: Expose only the operations named in this issue through the owning GraphQL or gRPC boundary.

dataOwnership: Keycloak owns HOST credentials, required actions and interactive sessions. Authentication owns invitation/lifecycle command audit and the minimal Keycloak subject projection; User owns the host profile and authorization subject.
stateMachine: Invitation is INVITED -> ACTIONS_PENDING -> ACTIVE; EXPIRED and CANCELLED are terminal for that invitation revision.
Only verified email plus completed required actions may produce ACTIVE; browser redirect alone cannot activate.

dataPartitions: ADMIN organization or explicitly granted SITE/BRANCH partition; HOST callers cannot invite themselves.
fieldGroups: ACCOUNT_SUMMARY by default; PII_CONTACT and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit grants.

failureSemantics: Reject duplicate or malformed email, unauthorized scope, reused idempotency key with a different body and invalid state using stable codes without revealing unrelated accounts.

If Keycloak create succeeds but local commit or email action dispatch is uncertain, retain a visible reconciliation state and repair by exact realm plus subject/email; never create a second user blindly.
Never log action links, passwords, tokens, cookies or unmasked host PII.
idempotencyConcurrency: Require an idempotency key for commands that can be retried externally and persist its request fingerprint and result.
Use aggregate version compare-and-swap so concurrent writers produce one winner and a stable conflict for losers.
Deduplicate consumed events by event ID and business key.
